title: Top economist Steve Hanke told us why he thinks AI won't take all jobs
excerpt: Steve Hanke said simple economics explains why companies "won't be firing everybody and replacing them with AI."
content_html:
Top economist Steve Hanke told us why he doubts AI will be the job destroyer many expect

By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The idea that artificial intelligence will be free to use and virtually costless to provide is delusional and dumb, Steve Hanke says.

"This belief is based on a disconnect from reality, as well as a good dose of idiotic economic reasoning," the professor of applied economics at Johns Hopkins University told Business Insider by email.

"AI is incredibly costly; it is very resource intensive," Hanke continued. "It requires huge amounts of water, power, and physical capital" like graphics chips, he added.

Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta have projected roughly $700 billion in combined capital expenditures this year, and $1 trillion in 2027, as they race to build out the data centers needed to power the next generation of AI models.

Hanke, who served on President Reagan's Council of Economic Advisers, also addressed widespread concerns that AI will cause massive job destruction.

"Businesses will not be firing everybody and replacing them with AI," he said, because in many cases that will be a lot more expensive than employing humans.

The veteran economist took aim at AI visionaries, describing many of them as "charlatans and hucksters." He said they're "comparing apples and oranges" when they liken AI to software, as providing AI to customers costs money whereas software, once developed, can be sold countless times at virtually no additional cost.

Hanke predicted the "cost of scarce resources that are gobbled up by AI will decide how far the 'AI revolution' goes."

AI optimists have countered that technological advances will make microchips and data centers more power-efficient over time, bringing down the cost of AI.

Elon Musk has made waves for predicting that AI will supercharge productivity and drive down production costs, ushering in an era of abundance where "anyone can have whatever stuff they want."

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO has recommended people stop saving for retirement in 10 or 20 years as "money won't matter." Personal finance and AI experts previously told Business Insider they resoundingly disagreed with Musk's advice.

Musk has predicted AI will take over most jobs, and the "best way" for governments to deal with the resulting unemployment is to provide a "universal high income" by mailing checks to everyone.

Mounting concerns about AI

Hanke has been skeptical of AI for a while, describing it to Business Insider in February as "overhyped and potentially dangerous."

Last fall, Hanke said the AI boom could falter if Big Tech companies failed to hit their numbers, and said it "might be wise to buckle your seat belt."

Mark Cuban, the former "Shark Tank" investor, and Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame warned this week about the massive scale of AI spending and Nvidia's key role in financing it, underlining Hanke's concern about how much the technology costs.

Cuban said it was "truly scary" how central Nvidia is to the AI boom, and cautioned it "all could crumble" if the chipmaker gets outcompeted or makes a mistake.

Burry said Nvidia was "overreaching" in its campaign to strike deals with customers to support its chip sales, and its efforts threatened to "push the circular spending to biblical proportions."

content_html_zh:
顶级经济学家史蒂夫·汉克（Steve Hanke）告诉我们，为什么他怀疑人工智能是否会成为许多人期望的就业破坏者

作者：Theron Mohamed 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

史蒂夫·汉克表示，认为人工智能可以免费使用且几乎无成本提供的想法是妄想和愚蠢的。

“这种信念是基于与现实的脱节，以及大量愚蠢的经济推理，”约翰·霍普金斯大学应用经济学教授通过电子邮件告诉《商业内幕》。

汉克继续说道：“人工智能的成本极其高昂；它是资源密集型的。” 他补充说，“这需要大量的水、电力和图形芯片等实物资本”。

微软、Alphabet、亚马逊和 Meta 预计今年的总资本支出约为 7000 亿美元，到 2027 年将达到 1 万亿美元，因为它们竞相建设为下一代人工智能模型提供动力所需的数据中心。

曾在里根总统的经济顾问委员会任职的汉克还谈到了人们普遍担心人工智能将导致大规模就业机会消失的担忧。

他说：“企业不会解雇所有人并用人工智能取代他们，”因为在许多情况下，这比雇用人类要昂贵得多。

这位资深经济学家将矛头指向人工智能梦想家，将他们中的许多人描述为“江湖骗子和小贩”。 他表示，当他们将人工智能比作软件时，他们是在“比较苹果和橘子”，因为向客户提供人工智能需要花钱，而软件一旦开发出来，就可以无数次销售，几乎不需要额外成本。

汉克预测，“被人工智能吞噬的稀缺资源的成本将决定‘人工智能革命’能走多远。”

人工智能乐观主义者反驳说，随着时间的推移，技术进步将使微芯片和数据中心更加节能，从而降低人工智能的成本。

埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）预测人工智能将提高生产力并降低生产成本，从而迎来一个“任何人都可以拥有他们想要的任何东西”的丰富时代，这引起了轰动。

这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 的首席执行官建议人们在 10 或 20 年内停止为退休储蓄，因为“钱不重要”。 个人理财和人工智能专家此前告诉《商业内幕》，他们坚决不同意马斯克的建议。

马斯克预测人工智能将接管大部分工作，而政府应对由此产生的失业的“最佳方式”是通过向每个人邮寄支票来提供“普遍高收入”。

人们对人工智能的担忧日益加剧

一段时间以来，汉克一直对人工智能持怀疑态度，他在二月份向《商业内幕》描述人工智能“被过度炒作且存在潜在危险”。

去年秋天，汉克表示，如果大型科技公司未能达到预期目标，人工智能的繁荣可能会陷入停滞，并表示“系好安全带可能是明智之举”。

《创智赢家》前投资者马克·库班和因《大空头》而闻名的迈克尔·伯里本周对人工智能支出的大规模以及英伟达在融资方面的关键作用发出警告，这突显了汉克对技术成本的担忧。

库班表示，英伟达在人工智能热潮中的核心地位“确实令人恐惧”，并警告说，如果这家芯片制造商在竞争中被击败或犯了错误，“一切都可能崩溃”。

伯里表示，英伟达在与客户达成交易以支持其芯片销售方面“过度”，其努力可能会“将循环支出推至神圣的比例”。
